correctness.rationale: Brownian scaling makes each completed reward Y=tau^rho*xi, with rho=1+beta/2. At exactly Pareto exponent rho, tau^rho has the law U^{-1}. Conditioning gives P(Y>x)=E[min(1,xi/x)] and the truncated mean b(x)=E[xi log(x/xi) 1_{xi<=x}]. E xi=4/((2+beta)sqrt(pi)), xP(Y>x)->E xi, and b(x)=E xi log x-E[xi log xi]+o(1). Index-one Lévy convergence with centering n b(n) follows by truncated characteristic functions. Renewal inversion for p-moments 1<p<rho, a count window n^q with 1/p<q<1, and a reward union/Markov bound make the random count o_P(n) at stable scale despite cycle length/reward dependence. Renewal backward-age tightness makes the unfinished area O_P(1). Independent Borel–Cantelli events Y_j>m j log j, plus T_j/j->mu, yield infinite a.s. limsup. This proves the stated full physical-time, all t->infinity claim; not a moment heuristic.
